assertions.name: 1_stored_and_live_agree_within_anchor_precision
assertions.detail: gap 0.07694 ppb = 0.06289 sigma of the muon anchor's own 1.223 ppb. Below 1 sigma the stored and live values are the same measurement. Above it, something moved that the anchor's precision does not explain -- a new CODATA edition, or an edit to the stored string.

description: Drift detection for the muon pin without the drift. The stored value is a fixed point (stable but unfalsifiable); the live derivation follows CODATA (checkable but silently drifting, which is how a stale-edition muon value reached 65 sites). This reports the gap in units of the muon anchor's OWN uncertainty, so a CODATA adjustment becomes visible instead of silent. It changes no pin and rules nothing -- A-vs-C is an owner decision.
computation_method: Compares _q0_value_for_anchor('muon') against q_muon_at(50), and propagates the CODATA m_mu/m_e uncertainty to sigma(q0) by a two-sided difference on the exact closed form. All mpmath at dps=60; no float64 -- a 0.08 ppb gap measured in float64 would be reporting its own arithmetic.
q0AnchorReason: Reads the muon pin (stored) and the proton pin on purpose -- the comparison IS the subject. Recorded under q0Values so each leg is checkable against its canonical value, per the `comparison` vocabulary.
scope: scope-(a) MEASUREMENT + gate. Changes no pin, wires nothing, and does not rule A-vs-C (bean qou-bred, owner decision). It only makes the disagreement observable.

result.verdict: At 0.063 sigma the stored and live muon pins are the same measurement -- no framework observable distinguishes them, and no prediction depends on the A-vs-C choice. That is why this is a governance ruling and not a physics one.

context.recommendation: step 3 of the A-vs-C brief on qou-bred
